questions.stem: This midsagittal diagram of the head and neck labels the epiglottis at the entrance to the larynx. What is its primary function?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Covering the laryngeal opening during swallowing

explanation.summary: During swallowing the epiglottis folds back over the laryngeal inlet, directing food into the esophagus and protecting the airway from aspiration.
explanation.whyCorrect: During swallowing the epiglottis folds back over the laryngeal inlet, directing food into the esophagus and protecting the airway from aspiration.

questions.stem: This cadaveric midsagittal section of the head is used to highlight the olfactory epithelium. Which region of the respiratory tract is being displayed?

explanation.summary: The section shows the nasal septum and conchae of the nasal cavity, where the olfactory epithelium sits in the roof.
explanation.whyCorrect: The section shows the nasal septum and conchae of the nasal cavity, where the olfactory epithelium sits in the roof.

questions.stem: This airway wall shows a mucosa of tall pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium, a submucosa, and an underlying plate of pale hyaline cartilage with chondrocytes in lacunae. Which structure is this section most consistent with?

explanation.summary: Pseudostratified ciliated columnar (respiratory) epithelium resting on a mucosa/submucosa supported by hyaline cartilage is characteristic of the trachea and large bronchi of the conducting airways.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pseudostratified ciliated columnar (respiratory) epithelium resting on a mucosa/submucosa supported by hyaline cartilage is characteristic of the trachea and large bronchi of the conducting airways.

questions.stem: A small airway with folded epithelium is encircled by a layer of smooth muscle and surrounded by thin-walled air spaces (alveoli), with no cartilage present. What airway is shown?

explanation.summary: A small conducting airway lacking cartilage and glands but wrapped by a relatively prominent smooth muscle layer, surrounded by alveoli, identifies a bronchiole; the absence of cartilage distinguishes it from bronchi.
explanation.whyCorrect: A small conducting airway lacking cartilage and glands but wrapped by a relatively prominent smooth muscle layer, surrounded by alveoli, identifies a bronchiole; the absence of cartilage distinguishes it from bronchi.

questions.imageRef: repic-139_Brick Exchange - Histology of the Respiratory Tract_p15_1.png

questions.stem: This lung section (40X) shows a large conducting airway lined by pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium. What is the primary function of this epithelial lining?

explanation.summary: The bronchial epithelium is pseudostratified ciliated columnar with goblet cells; cilia sweep mucus-trapped debris up toward the pharynx (mucociliary escalator). Gas exchange occurs only in alveoli, not conducting airways.
explanation.whyCorrect: The bronchial epithelium is pseudostratified ciliated columnar with goblet cells; cilia sweep mucus-trapped debris up toward the pharynx (mucociliary escalator). Gas exchange occurs only in alveoli, not conducting airways.

questions.imageRef: repic-140_Brick Exchange - Histology of the Respiratory Tract_p16_1.png

questions.stem: This lung histology is labeled with a respiratory bronchiole (RB), alveolar ducts (AD), alveolar sacs (AS), and alveoli (A). Which functional zone of the respiratory system does this region represent?

choices.label: E
choices.text: The bronchial tree proximal to terminal bronchioles

explanation.summary: Respiratory bronchioles, alveolar ducts, sacs, and alveoli make up the respiratory zone where gas exchange occurs, distinguishing it from the purely conducting airways.
explanation.whyCorrect: Respiratory bronchioles, alveolar ducts, sacs, and alveoli make up the respiratory zone where gas exchange occurs, distinguishing it from the purely conducting airways.

questions.stem: In this diagram of an alveolus, what is the principal function of the Type 2 pneumocyte?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Forming the thin barrier for gas diffusion

choices.label: E
choices.text: Conducting air toward the alveolar duct

explanation.summary: Type 2 pneumocytes (cuboidal cells) secrete surfactant, which reduces surface tension and prevents alveolar collapse. Type 1 pneumocytes form the thin gas-exchange surface, and dust cells (macrophages) clear debris.
explanation.whyCorrect: Type 2 pneumocytes (cuboidal cells) secrete surfactant, which reduces surface tension and prevents alveolar collapse. Type 1 pneumocytes form the thin gas-exchange surface, and dust cells (macrophages) clear debris.

questions.stem: This H&E section shows thin-walled air spaces lined by Type 1 and Type 2 pneumocytes with an alveolar macrophage. From which organ is this tissue taken?

explanation.summary: The delicate alveolar architecture with Type 1/Type 2 pneumocytes and macrophages is characteristic of lung parenchyma.
explanation.whyCorrect: The delicate alveolar architecture with Type 1/Type 2 pneumocytes and macrophages is characteristic of lung parenchyma.

questions.stem: At the edge of this lung section a thin fibrous membrane (bracketed) covers the alveolar tissue. What is the functional role of this membrane?

explanation.summary: The visceral pleura is a serous membrane covering the lung; together with the parietal pleura and pleural fluid it minimizes friction as the lung expands and recoils during breathing.
explanation.whyCorrect: The visceral pleura is a serous membrane covering the lung; together with the parietal pleura and pleural fluid it minimizes friction as the lung expands and recoils during breathing.

questions.stem: This high-power view shows the epithelium that lines the trachea, with an apical row of cilia and a basal lamina propria. What is its main functional role?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Moving a mucus layer with trapped particles

explanation.summary: Pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium with goblet cells lines the trachea; coordinated ciliary beating propels mucus and trapped debris upward (mucociliary escalator).
explanation.whyCorrect: Pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium with goblet cells lines the trachea; coordinated ciliary beating propels mucus and trapped debris upward (mucociliary escalator).

questions.imageRef: repic-145_Brick Exchange - Histology of the Respiratory Tract_p3_1.png

questions.stem: This specialized pseudostratified epithelium in the roof of the nasal cavity contains bipolar sensory neurons (ON) among supporting (S) and basal (B) cells. What special sense does it mediate?

explanation.summary: The olfactory epithelium contains bipolar olfactory receptor neurons whose cilia detect odorants; supporting (sustentacular) and basal cells complete the epithelium.
explanation.whyCorrect: The olfactory epithelium contains bipolar olfactory receptor neurons whose cilia detect odorants; supporting (sustentacular) and basal cells complete the epithelium.

questions.stem: This diagram maps epithelial types onto the upper airway, showing stratified squamous epithelium in the oropharynx rather than ciliated epithelium. Why is stratified squamous epithelium found there?

choices.label: C
choices.text: To absorb nutrients from swallowed food

choices.label: D
choices.text: To improve ciliary clearance of particles

choices.label: E
choices.text: To maximize gas exchange with blood

explanation.summary: The oropharynx is a shared food and air passage; stratified squamous epithelium resists the abrasion of food boluses, unlike the delicate ciliated epithelium of purely respiratory passages.
explanation.whyCorrect: The oropharynx is a shared food and air passage; stratified squamous epithelium resists the abrasion of food boluses, unlike the delicate ciliated epithelium of purely respiratory passages.

questions.imageRef: repic-147_Brick Exchange - Histology of the Respiratory Tract_p7_1.png

questions.stem: This respiratory epithelium contains ciliated columnar cells, basal cells, and goblet cells. What is the role of the goblet cells?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Beating rhythmically to propel the mucus layer

choices.label: B
choices.text: Secreting mucus that traps inhaled particles

choices.label: C
choices.text: Carrying out gas exchange with capillaries

choices.label: D
choices.text: Serving as stem cells to regenerate the epithelium

explanation.summary: Goblet cells secrete mucus that traps debris and microbes; the cilia of columnar cells then sweep this mucus toward the pharynx, while basal cells act as the regenerative reserve.
explanation.whyCorrect: Goblet cells secrete mucus that traps debris and microbes; the cilia of columnar cells then sweep this mucus toward the pharynx, while basal cells act as the regenerative reserve.

questions.imageRef: repic-148_Brick Exchange - Histology of the Respiratory Tract_p8_1.png

questions.stem: This nonkeratinizing stratified epithelium overlying a lamina propria lines a region shared by the digestive and respiratory tracts. Which region is it most likely from?

explanation.summary: Nonkeratinizing stratified squamous epithelium lines areas subject to abrasion such as the oropharynx and laryngopharynx, protecting against the passage of food.
explanation.whyCorrect: Nonkeratinizing stratified squamous epithelium lines areas subject to abrasion such as the oropharynx and laryngopharynx, protecting against the passage of food.

questions.stem: This diagram shows O2 and CO2 crossing the structure between alveolar air and blood. By what mechanism do these gases cross this barrier?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Secondary active transport coupled to sodium

choices.label: D
choices.text: Osmosis of dissolved gas with water

explanation.summary: Gas exchange across the blood-air barrier is passive: O2 and CO2 diffuse down their respective partial pressure gradients through the thin Type 1 pneumocyte, fused basement membrane, and capillary endothelium.
explanation.whyCorrect: Gas exchange across the blood-air barrier is passive: O2 and CO2 diffuse down their respective partial pressure gradients through the thin Type 1 pneumocyte, fused basement membrane, and capillary endothelium.
